dataset.title: EC2 CPU Utilisation
dataset.description: CPU utilisation of a production EC2 instance fronting the public API. Contains two curated anomaly windows.

notes: 38 observation(s) exceed |robust z| > 4.0; retained as signal, flagged for review.

decomposition.interpretation: Seasonality is weak, so the series behaves closer to a noisy level process than to a repeating daily profile. The trend component is strong, indicating slow drift in the operating level over the observation window.

adf.null_hypothesis: A unit root is present (series is non-stationary).

kpss.null_hypothesis: The series is stationary around a constant level.
kpss.p_value_note: KPSS p-values are interpolated from a lookup table and are reported at the boundary when the statistic falls outside it.

verdict.label: non-stationary
verdict.explanation: ADF cannot reject a unit root and KPSS rejects stationarity. Both tests agree the level wanders, so first differencing (d = 1) is indicated.

correlation.interpretation: The PACF falls inside the +/-0.053 band after lag 3 and the ACF after lag 3, which is the evidence for the candidate orders p = 3, q = 3 carried into model selection. A slowly decaying ACF would instead indicate differencing is required first.

seasonality.interpretation: Load peaks around 17:00 and bottoms out around 12:00 UTC. A fixed threshold calibrated at the peak would be blind to an incident at the trough, which is the core argument for seasonal modelling.

Rolling volatility is far from constant, so the variance itself changes over time. A detector with a fixed global threshold will over-alert in volatile stretches and under-alert in calm ones; this motivates the rolling robust scale used throughout.

split.rationale: Random splitting would leak future information through the series' own autocorrelation, so the hold-out is strictly the tail of the timeline.

models.name: rolling_zscore
models.description: Classical statistical process control: a trailing window supplies a robust median and MAD-scaled spread, and any point beyond the sigma threshold is alerted.
models.rationale: The method most monitoring stacks ship by default. It has no notion of time-of-day, so it is included to quantify the cost of ignoring seasonality: it tends to alert every night when load legitimately collapses, and to miss daytime incidents hidden inside the peak.

models.name: hybrid
models.description: Two-stage forecast - SARIMAX with Fourier seasonality, corrected by a nonlinear learner trained on its residuals - feeding a dual detector that fuses a train-calibrated robust residual z-score with an Isolation Forest over residual-shape features, then debounces.
models.rationale: Each stage exists because a measured weakness of the previous one demanded it. SARIMAX leaves structured residuals; the nonlinear stage absorbs them. A magnitude threshold alone misses slow ramps; the residual-shape forest catches them. Raw thresholding alarms constantly; the debounce trades one bucket of latency for a large reduction in false pages.

diagnostics.interpretation: The nonlinear stage removed 70.3% of the variance the linear model left in its residuals. A figure near zero would be evidence that SARIMAX had already extracted everything predictable and that the hybrid is unnecessary complexity for this series - which is a legitimate finding, not a failure.

models.name: hybrid_neural
models.description: The same two-stage architecture with a feed-forward neural network (or an LSTM where PyTorch is installed) in place of gradient boosting at the residual-correction stage.
models.rationale: An ablation of the residual learner. If this and the boosted variant score alike, the gain is architectural; if they diverge sharply, the choice of learner is doing the work and should be tuned per series.

residual_learner.label: Feed-forward neural network (64-32, ReLU)
residual_learner.fallback_reason: PyTorch is not installed, so the LSTM residual stage fell back to the feed-forward network. Install torch to enable it.

diagnostics.interpretation: The nonlinear stage removed 45.9% of the variance the linear model left in its residuals. A figure near zero would be evidence that SARIMAX had already extracted everything predictable and that the hybrid is unnecessary complexity for this series - which is a legitimate finding, not a failure.

models.name: sarimax_fourier
models.description: ARMA(p, d, q) dynamics estimated jointly with harmonic regressors for the daily cycle. Order selected by AIC over a candidate grid informed by the ACF/PACF cut-offs.
models.rationale: A direct seasonal ARIMA is impractical here: at 15-minute resolution the daily period is 96, so SARIMA(p,d,q)(P,D,Q)[96] would require 96 seasonal lags from roughly 900 training observations. Encoding the cycle as four Fourier harmonic pairs captures the same periodic shape in eight coefficients and leaves the ARMA part to model only the short-memory dynamics it is good at.

diagnostics.residual_autocorrelation_note: A Ljung-Box p-value above 0.05 means no residual autocorrelation remains at lag 24, i.e. the linear structure has been adequately extracted.

models.name: holt_winters
models.description: Exponential smoothing state-space model with additive error, damped additive trend and additive daily seasonality; alerts on the robust z-score of the one-step-ahead residual.
models.rationale: Chosen because the EDA shows a strong, stable daily profile with slow level drift, which is exactly the structure ETS encodes. Damping the trend prevents the multi-step forecast from extrapolating a short local slope into an implausible ramp.

models.name: isolation_forest
models.description: Unsupervised ensemble of random isolation trees over a causal feature window (lags, rolling moments, differences and calendar context). Anomaly score is the negated path-depth decision function.
models.rationale: Included as the representative pure machine-learning detector. It assumes neither normality nor a generative model, so it can catch multivariate-shaped oddities - an ordinary level reached at an extraordinary rate, say - that a univariate residual threshold will miss. The trade-off is that it yields no forecast and therefore no capacity-planning value, and its scores are hard to explain to an on-call engineer.

models.name: seasonal_naive
models.description: Predicts each value from the observation exactly one seasonal period earlier, then alerts on a robust z-score of the residual.
models.rationale: The reference point for the whole comparison. MASE is defined against this model, so any method with MASE >= 1 has not earned its complexity. On diurnal infrastructure telemetry it is a genuinely strong baseline, not a straw man.

forecast_future.method: SARIMAX multi-step forecast with 95% prediction interval

incidents.summary: Variance changed sharply while the mean held.
incidents.recommended_action: Look for contention rather than load: noisy neighbours, lock or GC pauses, a flapping dependency, or an unhealthy member of the pool. Mean-based alerting will not catch a recurrence; keep the shape channel enabled.
incidents.headline: Volatility change: peak 54.90 %, +38% against forecast, sustained 165 min.

incidents.summary: Sustained displacement with no return to the prior baseline.
incidents.recommended_action: Treat as a change event until proven otherwise: inspect the deploy timeline, configuration changes, autoscaling actions and failovers at the window start. If the new level is intended, retrain the baseline so it stops paging.
incidents.headline: Level shift: peak 38.36 %, -11% against forecast, sustained 90 min.

incidents.summary: Short, sharp collapse below the expected level.
incidents.recommended_action: Check for an upstream outage, a failed health check pulling the node out of rotation, or an agent that stopped reporting. A dip to exactly zero usually means missing telemetry, not idle capacity.
incidents.headline: Dip: peak 37.35 %, -2% against forecast, sustained 30 min.

narrative.headline: Rolling Z-Score (3-sigma) selected for api-gateway-prod-01
points: Rolling Z-Score (3-sigma) ranks first with a composite operational score of 0.858, recovering 1/1 labelled incident window(s) at a point-adjusted F1 of 1.000.
Mean time to first alert inside an incident is 465 minutes, at 0.00 false alarm(s) per day.
That is +0.172 against the seasonal-naive baseline, so the modelling effort is justified on this series.
The nonlinear stage removed 70.3% of the variance remaining in the linear model's residuals, which is the direct measure of what hybridisation bought.
